AccessTokenResponse.description: A bearer token returned by a successful local sign-in.
AccessTokenResponse.title: AccessTokenResponse

BuilderOperationCreateInput.description: One new operation within a job definition being created.
BuilderOperationCreateInput.title: BuilderOperationCreateInput

BuilderOperationReplaceInput.description: One operation within a replacement. Send an id to retain it; omit it for a new operation.
BuilderOperationReplaceInput.title: BuilderOperationReplaceInput

BuilderRouteInput.description: What it costs one machine to run one operation, as the builder edits it.
BuilderRouteInput.title: BuilderRouteInput

CapabilityUpsertRequest.description:
What it costs this machine to run one operation.

duration is occupancy in minutes and is always required -- an operation cannot be sequenced
without one. energy stays optional for the same reason salary does.
CapabilityUpsertRequest.title: CapabilityUpsertRequest

CurrentUserResponse.description: The safe subset of the signed-in account exposed to the frontend.
CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse

DependencyEdgeRequest.description: One ordering edge: `before` must finish before `after` starts.
DependencyEdgeRequest.title: DependencyEdgeRequest

JobCreateRequest.description:
A job a manager is adding to the backlog.

Only a name: the operations inside a job are added separately, and job names are deliberately
not unique because two real jobs can carry the same description. Priority is not settable here
yet -- every job is created at the database default until the job-definition endpoint (#235)
exists.
JobCreateRequest.title: JobCreateRequest

JobDefinitionCreateRequest.description: A complete job a manager is creating in one request: its priority and every operation.
JobDefinitionCreateRequest.title: JobDefinitionCreateRequest

JobDefinitionReplaceRequest.description:
A complete replacement for one job's definition.

The array index of each operation is its 1-based position -- there is no caller-controlled
position field, so drag-reorder has one unambiguous representation.
JobDefinitionReplaceRequest.title: JobDefinitionReplaceRequest

JobDefinitionResponse.description: The canonical shape of a job definition: everything the builder needs to redraw it.
JobDefinitionResponse.title: JobDefinitionResponse

JobDependenciesReplaceRequest.description:
The complete ordering for one job, replacing whatever is currently stored.

A job's ordering is every edge whose `after_operation_id` is one of its own operations, so this
can express a step waiting on an operation in a different job -- allowed on purpose -- while
still leaving every edge owned by exactly one job.
JobDependenciesReplaceRequest.title: JobDependenciesReplaceRequest

JobDependencyEdgeResponse.description: One job that has to finish before another can start.
JobDependencyEdgeResponse.title: JobDependencyEdgeResponse

JobDependencyGraphResponse.description:
Which jobs wait on which, across the whole backlog.

Derived from `dependencies`, which joins operations rather than jobs: an edge appears here
only when its two operations belong to different jobs. Edges inside a single job order that
job's own steps and are read through `GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/dependencies` instead.

Deliberately the whole graph in one response rather than a field on each job in the paginated
job list. A job's prerequisites can sit on any page, and computing them per row would mean
walking the dependency graph once per job on every page read. The payload is one row per
cross-job edge, of which there are usually none.
JobDependencyGraphResponse.title: JobDependencyGraphResponse

JobDetailResponse.description: A single job with the operations it contains, in position order.
JobDetailResponse.title: JobDetailResponse

JobOperationResponse.description: An operation as seen from its job. Managed through the operations API, not here.
JobOperationResponse.title: JobOperationResponse

JobUpdateRequest.description:
A partial update. `name` is NOT NULL, so an explicit null is rejected rather than stored.

`archived` retires the job from the backlog (`true`) or brings it back (`false`). It is a
boolean here rather than the timestamp the row stores, because the caller decides *whether* the
job is archived and the server records *when*.
JobUpdateRequest.title: JobUpdateRequest

MachineCreateRequest.description:
A machine a manager is adding to the floor.

category_id and salary are optional: nothing in the scheduler reads a machine's category, and a
machine with no recorded salary is excluded from a schedule's labour total rather than counted
as free. Requiring either would block entering a machine whose details are not settled yet.
MachineCreateRequest.title: MachineCreateRequest

MachineDetailResponse.description: A single machine with the operations it is declared able to run.
MachineDetailResponse.title: MachineDetailResponse

MachineUpdateRequest.description:
A partial update. An omitted field is left alone; an explicit null clears it.

Only the nullable columns may be cleared. `name` and `active` are NOT NULL, so an explicit null
for either is rejected here rather than reaching the database as an integrity error.
MachineUpdateRequest.title: MachineUpdateRequest

OperationCompatibilityResponse.description: What one machine costs for this operation. Managed through the capability endpoints.
OperationCompatibilityResponse.title: OperationCompatibilityResponse

OperationCreateRequest.description:
A step a manager is adding to a job.

Only a name. What the step costs is a property of the machine that runs it and is recorded
through the capability endpoints, and where it sits in the order is recorded through the job's
dependencies -- neither is a field on the step itself.
OperationCreateRequest.title: OperationCreateRequest

OperationDetailResponse.description:
One operation with its machine options and its place in the ordering.

`predecessors` and `successors` are operation ids rather than full edges: one end of every such
edge is this operation, so repeating it would say nothing.
OperationDetailResponse.title: OperationDetailResponse

OperationUpdateRequest.description: A partial update. `name` is NOT NULL, so an explicit null is rejected rather than stored.
OperationUpdateRequest.title: OperationUpdateRequest

ScheduleCreateRequest.description:
Request a draft schedule from the current floor configuration.

`job_ids` scopes the run to a chosen part of the backlog (#231). Omitting it plans the whole
floor, which is what this request has always meant, so no existing caller changes behaviour.

A selection is validated where the dependency graph is already being read, not here: an unknown
job, a selection with no schedulable work, and a selection missing a job that a selected job
waits on each come back through the generation status resource as a `rejected` outcome with its
own issue code. See `GET /api/v1/jobs/dependency-graph` for working out what a selection
implies before sending one.
ScheduleCreateRequest.title: ScheduleCreateRequest

ScheduleGenerationAcceptedResponse.description: A queued generation command and the resource used to observe it.
ScheduleGenerationAcceptedResponse.title: ScheduleGenerationAcceptedResponse

ScheduleGenerationStatusResponse.description:
The externally visible state of one queued schedule-generation command.

Terminal operational failures include a safe, API-authored detail. It is
intentionally not a worker exception: clients can show it directly while
operational diagnostics remain in worker logs.
ScheduleGenerationStatusResponse.title: ScheduleGenerationStatusResponse

ScheduleSummaryResponse.description:
One schedule without its entries, for choosing between them.

A schedule's entries and dependency graph run to hundreds of rows each, so
the collection answers summaries and a caller fetches the one it wants.
ScheduleSummaryResponse.title: ScheduleSummaryResponse

SchedulingIssueResponse.description:
One unsupported or invalid scheduling input reported by the adapter.

At most one of the three ids is set, naming whichever the issue is about, so a client can mark
the offending row rather than parse `message`.
SchedulingIssueResponse.title: SchedulingIssueResponse

SimulationCreateRequest.description: Create the simulation for a confirmed schedule.
SimulationCreateRequest.title: SimulationCreateRequest

SimulationEventRequest.description:
Record one playback control action.

``speed`` is required for ``started``, ``resumed`` and ``speed_changed``, and
ignored otherwise.
SimulationEventRequest.title: SimulationEventRequest

SimulationResponse.description:
A simulation and the position derived from its event log.

``simulated_time`` is a derived measurement in the schedule's own units, so it
is a float rather than an exact decimal. ``speed`` mirrors the stored
``Numeric(5, 2)`` column and stays a decimal.
SimulationResponse.title: SimulationResponse

TimelineLaneResponse.description: A machine lane or job row, identified by key and shown by label.
TimelineLaneResponse.title: TimelineLaneResponse

TimelineOperationResponse.description: One scheduled operation, ready to draw as a bar.
TimelineOperationResponse.title: TimelineOperationResponse

TimelineResponse.description:
A schedule resolved onto the clock.

Machines and jobs are listed separately from operations so a renderer can lay
out lanes and rows without scanning every operation to discover them.

The payload is immutable for a confirmed schedule: the same entries and
dependencies always resolve to the same times, so a client may fetch it once
and animate locally against it.
TimelineResponse.title: TimelineResponse

409.description: A category already uses that name

get.description:
List the backlog's jobs with their operations and routes, a page at a time.

Lists every operation and route in this page in bulk, so the frontend has no N+1 detail fetch.
Archived jobs are left out unless `include_archived` is set, matching `GET /api/v1/jobs`.

post.description:
Create one job, its operations and their machine routes in a single transaction.

A failed validation writes nothing: no job, operation or compatibility row exists unless every
route names an active machine.

422.description: A route names an unknown or inactive machine

get.description:
List the backlog by name, a page at a time.

Archived jobs are left out unless `include_archived` is set: they have finished or been
cancelled and are no longer offered for scheduling, but they still exist because the schedules
that planned them do.

post.description: Add a job to the backlog. Its operations are added separately.

get.description:
Read every cross-job precedence edge, so a caller can tell what selecting a job implies.

Scoped schedule generation refuses a selection that leaves out a job a selected job waits on
(#231). This is how a caller works that out before sending one: take the jobs the manager
ticked, follow these edges backwards, and tick whatever they land on. Following them forwards
would pull in jobs that merely wait on the selection, which do not have to be scheduled with it.

The whole graph, unpaginated, because it is one row per cross-job edge and a job's prerequisites
are not confined to any one page of `GET /api/v1/jobs`.
get.summary: Get which jobs wait on which

delete.description:
Remove a job entered by mistake, together with its operations.

A job whose operations appear in a schedule cannot be removed: the schedule records what was
planned, and deleting the job would destroy that history. The 409 names the schedules in the
way. Drafts among them can be deleted first; a confirmed schedule cannot, and the job is
archived instead (`PATCH` with `archived: true`). See decision 0015.

204.description: The job and its operations were removed

409.description: The job's work appears in a schedule; the body names the draft and confirmed schedules involved

get.description: Read one job together with the operations it contains.
get.summary: Get a job and its operations

patch.description:
Apply a partial update, so a later schedule is generated from the corrected job.

`archived: true` retires the job from the backlog by hand, for a job that finished without a
simulation running or one that was cancelled; `archived: false` brings it back. Neither touches
any schedule, and neither makes the job deletable.

get.description: Read a job's complete definition: its priority, its operations and their routes, in order.
get.summary: Read one job definition for editing

put.description:
Replace a job's name, priority, operations and routes wholesale, atomically.

Omit an existing operation's id to delete it; omit id entirely for a new operation. The array
index becomes each operation's 1-based position. Only this job's own `builder_sequence`
ordering edges are rebuilt; externally owned edges are never touched.

Refused with a conflict only when the save would remove an operation a generated schedule
already recorded; every other edit is covered by the schedule's own snapshot, so a scheduled
job stays editable. The conflict names the schedules in the way. An archived job is editable
too: archiving takes a job out of the backlog, it does not freeze it (decision 0015).

409.description: The save would remove an operation that appears in a schedule; the body names the draft and confirmed schedules involved

422.description: A route names an unknown or inactive machine, an operation id does not belong to this job, removing an operation would delete another job's edge to it, or the new ordering would form a cycle

get.description: Read a job's ordering: every edge its own operations wait on.
get.summary: Get the order a job's operations run in

put.description:
Replace a job's ordering with the one supplied, atomically.

The whole ordering is sent rather than one edge at a time because reordering is a single change:
applied edge by edge it would pass through graphs that may themselves be cyclic, and a failure
part-way would leave an order nobody asked for. Sending the whole graph also means the cycle
check is one question about one graph.

Idempotent, as `PUT` requires: re-sending the same ordering restates it.

422.description: An edge names an unknown operation, orders an operation belonging to another job, or the ordering would form a cycle

put.summary: Set the order a job's operations run in

post.description: Add a step to a job. Its durations and its ordering are recorded separately.
post.summary: Add an operation to a job

Apply a partial update, including decommissioning through `active`.

There is no delete: a machine with recorded history cannot be removed, so retiring one is a
status change. See the deletion policy in docs/database-schema.md.

put.description:
Create or replace one operation-machine pairing.

Idempotent, as `PUT` requires: re-sending a pairing restates its cost rather than failing.
put.summary: Declare what it costs this machine to run an operation

delete.description:
Remove a step entered by mistake, together with its capabilities and its ordering edges.

An operation that already appears in a schedule cannot be removed: the schedule records what was
planned, and deleting the step would destroy that history. See the deletion policy in
docs/database-schema.md.

204.description: The operation, its capabilities and its ordering were removed

409.description: The operation already appears in a schedule

get.description:
Read one operation with everything needed to edit it.

The capability rows are also reachable machine-first, but answering "what can run this step, and
how long does each take" from there would mean reading every machine on the floor.
get.summary: Get an operation, its machine options and its place in the order

patch.description: Apply a partial update, so a later schedule is generated from the corrected step.

get.description:
List every schedule, newest first, without its entries.

A caller that wants to open one has no other way to learn its identifier:
generation reports an id only to whoever queued it, and a seeded schedule
reports none at all. Summaries rather than full resources, because entries
and dependencies run to hundreds of rows per schedule.

schema.title: Response List Schedules Api V1 Schedules Get

post.description: Queue draft generation without running the scheduling policy in the API process.

get.description: Read a queued command's state with safe API-authored terminal details.

delete.description:
Throw away a draft nobody confirmed.

A draft blocks removal of the jobs and operations it planned until it is gone, which is the
usual reason to delete one: the manager generated it to look, then wants to change the job.
Only drafts can be deleted; a confirmed schedule is what the floor was told to do and stays,
together with any simulation of it (decision 0015).

204.description: The draft and everything recorded under it were removed

409.description: The schedule is confirmed or discarded, so it is history

get.description: Fetch one immutable schedule version with its entries and dependency graph.

Resolve a schedule's entries and dependencies into start and end times.

The result is immutable for a confirmed schedule, so a client should fetch it
once per schedule and animate locally rather than polling.
get.summary: Get a schedule resolved onto the clock

post.description:
Create the simulation for a confirmed schedule.

A schedule has at most one simulation; resetting re-initialises that row
rather than creating another, so a repeat request reports a conflict.

get.description: Derive where a simulation currently sits by replaying its event log.

post.description:
Append a control action and return the position it produces.

Control actions are a subordinate resource rather than verbs in the path, so
play, pause, resume, speed change, reset and completion all post here. The
`Location` header points at the simulation the action affected, since events
are not individually addressable.
